newsitem.title: USA: Hicks, Muse to buy Knight Quality for $70 million.
newsitem.headline: Hicks, Muse to buy Knight Quality for $70 million.

text.p: Hicks, Muse, Tate & Furst Inc. and Capstar Broadcasting Partners, a radio investment group formed by Hicks Muse, said Thursday they have signed a letter of intent to buy Knight Quality Stations in a deal valued at about $70 million.
Knight Quality Stations, established in 1959, has eight middle-market stations in New England.
The deal is expected to close in January, subject to the execution of a definitive agreement.
"This transaction brings the capital value of all acquisitions completed or announced since Capstar's formation (in May 1996) to approximately $855 million," the companies said.
N. Scott Knight, Knight's chief executive officer, and Robert Knight, the company's executive vice president, agreed to join Capstar's senior management team after the deal is completed.
Hicks Muse, based in Dallas, is a private investment firm with a total capital value of about $19 billion.
